clue.text: Harmony in East Anglian marketplace puts one off

indicators.note: the musical word sits within the name of the Norfolk town, so in marks a container

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, East Anglia
a concert is agreement or harmony, as in acting in concert

explanation.surface: Musical harmony in a Norfolk market square repels a visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: Diss is a small market town in Norfolk, in the East Anglia region of England; 'Harmony' looks like the subject of the sentence but is the inner piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To disconcert someone is to unsettle or fluster them, putting them off their stride.

parts.note: a line from Tennyson's Maud describing a yellow spring sky, completed by the name of a spring bulb

explanation.surface: A quotation from Tennyson with a word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson's Maud has 'On a bed of daffodil sky', the yellow of the spring flower.

parts.note: the name of a sea trout reads as if it crossed two kinds of fish

explanation.surface: A fish that is a cross between two species.
explanation.walkthrough: This sea trout is a single species, but its double name looks like a cross between two fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea trout is so called, its name joining two game fish as if a cross of both.

parts.note: in Homer's Odyssey the nymph Calypso keeps Odysseus on her island for seven years

explanation.surface: An island associated with calypso music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calypso' suggests Caribbean music; here it is the nymph of the Odyssey, whose island home held Odysseus.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer names the island home of the nymph Calypso, where Odysseus was held for seven years.

clue.text: Such a bind — this kind of letter !

explanation.surface: Someone groans that a certain kind of letter is a real nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A series of linked rings binds or fetters, and a letter asking each reader to copy it on to others is so named.

clue.text: Produces a neat finish, of course, when the game's cancelled

definitions.text: of course, when the game's cancelled

explanation.surface: Golf is called off, which neatly ends the day.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish something neatly is to complete it smoothly, and when golf is cancelled the circuits of the course are off.

parts.note: read as a ..., a supporter of a team, it names an assistant churchwarden who takes the collection

explanation.surface: A football fan seen in church.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as SIDE'S MAN it is a team's supporter; as one word it is an assistant to the churchwarden who shows people to pews.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant churchwarden who seats the congregation and takes the collection bears this title.

explanation.surface: A candle that is hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: A depression in the ground is a hollow, and a candle made by repeated dipping of a wick in tallow is also so named.

parts.note: in Dickens's Bleak House, Mr Jarndyce calls the private room he retreats to when out of humour the Growlery

explanation.surface: An alternative name for a room.
explanation.walkthrough: In Bleak House Mr Jarndyce names his private sitting room the Growlery, as a lion growls in its lair.
explanation.definitionFit: A private study or retreat, like a wild animal's lair, is what Dickens's Growlery is.

parts.note: earnest appeals, the word close to the polite word added to a request

explanation.surface: Asking nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: Appeals or entreaties are requests, and the word is the polite 'please' shortened.

clue.text: Would Buster make a buccaneer of her?

definitions.text: Would Buster make a buccaneer of her?

parts.words: Would Buster make a buccaneer of her?
parts.note: a young female horse put before the word buster sounds like filibuster, an old word for a freebooting pirate

explanation.surface: A man called Buster might turn a woman into a pirate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buster' looks like a man's name; it is the tail of FILIBUSTER, a freebooter or buccaneer, whose front sounds like a young mare.
explanation.definitionFit: A young female horse is the 'her' whose name, followed by buster, gives the word for a freebooter.

parts.note: a tea dance pictured as a dance with buns, read as one word, means plenty

explanation.surface: Someone asks the price of a ticket to an afternoon tea dance.
explanation.walkthrough: A thé dansant is a tea dance; split the answer as A BUN DANCE and it describes one, while the whole word answers 'how much?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenty, a great quantity, is the reply to 'how much?' that the split phrase also spells.

clue.text: Scot, 'oppressed by bull at the university ?

parts.note: a bull is an ox
something oppressed by a weight has that weight lying on it
Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A Scotsman at university is bullied by a large man.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian is a stock Scottish name; 'oppressed by' pictures the bull lying on top of him. The university is Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of Oxford University, its student or graduate, is called by this Latin-derived name.

clue.text: Is this what they do at those working luncheons?

definitions.text: Is this what they do at those working luncheons?

parts.words: Is this what they do at those working luncheons?
parts.note: at a business lunch people talk matters over, while the word also splits into a plate (disc) and a word sounding like a curse

explanation.surface: Wondering what really goes on at business lunches.
explanation.definitionFit: Talking a subject over is the stated purpose of a working meal.

parts.note: the process of joining separate parts so that they become a single whole

explanation.surface: Someone counting off the first of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That makes one' sounds like counting; it means the act that turns many into one.
explanation.definitionFit: Joining several parts into a single whole is the act of making one.

clue.text: One receives love and gratitude by letter

indicators.note: the numeral takes on the following pieces, so receives joins them after it

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
love is nil in tennis, the letter O
ta is British informal thanks

explanation.surface: Someone is sent love and thanks in the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by letter' looks like 'by post', but 'letter' is the definition: a Greek letter. TA is everyday British slang for 'thank you'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ninth character of the Greek alphabet bears this name.

clue.text: Colourful in a scaly kind of way ?

definitions.text: in a scaly kind of way

explanation.surface: Something brightly coloured like a lizard's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means highly coloured, and also describes a musical scale moving in semitones.

clue.text: Greeting-and what a state of affairs !

explanation.surface: Someone says hello and then exclaims at the mess they find.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned greeting on meeting someone, and also an informal phrase for an awkward predicament.

clue.text: Shakespeare's dullards, exemplified by Bottom perhaps?.

definitions.text: Shakespeare's dullards, exemplified by Bottom perhaps?.

parts.words: Shakespeare's dullards, exemplified by Bottom perhaps?.
parts.note: Shakespeare's term for little asses or fools in Troilus and Cressida; Bottom wears an ass's head in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's stupid characters, such as the weaver Bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: In Troilus and Cressida Thersites calls Ajax an asinico, a little ass; Bottom is turned into an ass in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's word for fools or dolts comes from the Spanish for a little donkey, and Bottom literally wore a donkey's head.

clue.text: Keeps on producing postscript about sister in trouble

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes round the jumbled word, so about marks a container

parts.note: PS is the abbreviation for a postscript at the end of a letter

indicators.note: a sister in trouble is disturbed, so her letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A letter writer keeps adding a postscript about a sister who is in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producing' is only a link; 'in trouble' scrambles the sister and 'about' wraps the postscript abbreviation around the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere or continue steadfastly is to carry on without stopping.

clue.text: The sailor keeps her in his quarters, not in every port !

definitions.text: The sailor keeps her in his quarters, not in every port !

parts.words: The sailor keeps her in his quarters, not in every port !
parts.note: not a girl in every port but a small sewing kit, which shares its name with a married woman at home

explanation.surface: A sailor with one woman kept in his cabin, unlike the proverbial girl in every port.
explanation.walkthrough: A sailor's sewing kit of needles and thread is traditionally given the same name as a woman who keeps a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact case of needles and thread carried by servicemen bears the same name as a homemaker.

parts.note: in the Gospel parable the poor widow gives a tiny coin, and a small child is also called by that word

explanation.surface: A widow and her little child.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Gospels a poor widow puts her small coin in the temple treasury; a small child is also called by that word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny coin of the parable and a small child share this name.

clue.text: Israel so named in marriage, according to Isaiah

definitions.text: Israel so named in marriage, according to Isaiah

parts.words: Israel so named in marriage, according to Isaiah
parts.note: Isaiah 62:4 says the land shall be called by a Hebrew name meaning married

explanation.surface: A biblical prophet's name for the land of Israel as a bride.
explanation.walkthrough: Isaiah 62:4 promises the land a new Hebrew name meaning 'married', for 'thy land shall be married'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Isaiah 62:4 the land of Israel is given this Hebrew name, meaning married.

parts.note: the title character of Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice, who borrows from Shylock

explanation.surface: A trader from Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's play The Merchant of Venice takes its title from this trader, who pledges a pound of flesh.

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the title of the novel, so in signals letters tucked within it

explanation.surface: Criminal activity in Trollope's novel about a country vicarage.
explanation.walkthrough: Framley Parsonage is a novel by Anthony Trollope; 'in' points to the run of letters within its second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a serious crime, once a felony.

parts.note: Aeschylus's Seven Against Thebes pits seven champions against the defenders of that Greek city

explanation.surface: The enemies of seven champions.
explanation.definitionFit: The citizens of Thebes defended their city against the Seven, in the Greek legend dramatised by Aeschylus.

clue.text: " Turn down an empty glass ", as the Italian poet might have put it ?

definitions.text: " Turn down an empty glass ", as the Italian poet might have put it ?

parts.words: " Turn down an empty glass ", as the Italian poet might have put it ?
parts.note: the last line of FitzGerald's Rubaiyat, where tass is an old word for a cup and an O suggests the empty glass upturned

explanation.surface: A line of verse recast as an Italian poet would phrase it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rubaiyat ends 'Turn down an empty Glass!'; a tass is a small cup, and adding O, a zero, makes the empty glass the name of Torquato, the epic poet of Jerusalem Delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian epic poet who wrote Jerusalem Delivered has a name that reads as a cup followed by nothing.

parts.note: not a feeling of irritation but the cogs round the rim of a wheel

explanation.surface: Something that sets one's teeth on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teeth on edge' wants to be irritation; it is the cogs on the rim of a wheel that grip a chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Projecting cogs round the rim of a wheel engage the links of a chain.

explanation.surface: Knitting something for one's spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The wife is so called from Eve, made from Adam's rib in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribbed stitch is a kind of knitting, and a wife is jocularly called by the bone Eve was made from.

parts.note: in biblical times a runner tucked up his robe and girded the lower back and hips before running

explanation.surface: Ancient athletes preparing for a race.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'gird up one's loins' is the biblical phrase for tucking up a robe to run, as Elijah did before running ahead of Ahab.
explanation.definitionFit: The lower back and hips are what a biblical runner girded up before setting off.

clue.text: What's the point, when there's no ball ?

definitions.text: What's the point, when there's no ball ?

parts.words: What's the point, when there's no ball ?
parts.note: a pen without a ballpoint writes through its metal tip

explanation.surface: Someone asking what the point is of a game with no ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's the point' sounds like a shrug; it asks for the writing tip of a pen that is not a ballpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: The writing tip of a fountain or dip pen is its point.

parts.note: an Old Testament wave-offering pictured as raised palms waving in a vote

explanation.surface: An offering waved before the altar, as in the Old Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: A wave-offering in Leviticus is a sacrifice waved before the altar; here the wave is hands raised to vote.
explanation.definitionFit: A vote taken by raising hands offers a wave of palms.
